summary: Credential translation audit for scheduled analytics jobs: GCP->AWS role binding failures
description: Issue summary: Several nightly analytics batch jobs that run on GKE using Workload Identity and then assume AWS roles for downstream S3/KMS access are intermittently failing with AccessDenied errors. Impact: A subset of non-critical analytics pipelines miss daily data windows (approx 10-20% of runs in the last 7 days). This is internal-only (no customer SLA breach yet) but increases alert noise and manual reruns. Scope: affects scheduler-triggered CronJobs in projects analytics-prod and analytics-staging that rely on the GCP->AWS credential translation layer (workload-identity -> STS assume-role).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Deploy a test CronJob to analytics-prod GKE cluster that uses annotated service account sa-analytics-worker@project.iam.gserviceaccount.com
2) Job runs container that requests AWS credentials via our token-exchange proxy (token-exchange.internal.svc): POST /v1/translate with Google identity token
3) Proxy calls STS AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity against AWS account:arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/analytics-crossaccount-role with web identity token
4) Observe response: HTTP 403 / AccessDenied or intermittent 200 with short-lived creds
5) Note the relationship between GCP token 'sub' claim and the Role trust condition in AWS (sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity)
observed_behavior: Token-exchange proxy returns 403 from AWS STS ~15% of the time. Logs show 'Not authorized to perform sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity' and 'Condition check failed: StringLike: sub' intermittently. When 403 occurs the scheduler retries and eventually succeeds on a later attempt or a manual rerun, but some downstream jobs are time-sensitive and miss windows.
expected_behavior: All scheduled jobs that present a valid GCP Workload Identity token that matches the AWS role trust condition should consistently receive temporary AWS credentials and proceed without human intervention.

investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: The AWS role trust policy uses a StringLike condition that expects a different token 'sub' format (project vs full email). Some tokens from GKE tokens are short-form (system:serviceaccount:... without domain) while Workload Identity can emit either 'sub' or 'email' depending on token audience/format.
Hypothesis 2: Token-exchange proxy occasionally caches an older token mapping from metadata server leading to stale 'sub' claim being presented.

Initial check: Pulled sampled GCP OIDC tokens from failing and successful runs and compared 'sub'/'email' claims. Failing tokens show 'sub' == 'system:serviceaccount:analytics:sa-analytics-worker' while successful ones include the project-scoped email form 'sa-analytics-worker@analytics-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com'.

AWS role trust policy currently: {"Effect":"Allow","Principal":{"Federated":"arn:aws:iam::123456789012:oidc-provider/token.actions.com"},"Condition":{"StringLike":{"token.actions.com:sub":"sa-analytics-worker@analytics-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com"}}} — which does not match the short-form 'system:serviceaccount' tokens.
Checked recent deploys: No recent changes to role trust policies; last update 2026-01-21 (INT-30421 referenced for readonly cloud-trace access) — role policy appears unchanged.

Checked token-exchange proxy: code first added normalization on 2025-11 but a race exists when token source is GKE metadata vs Workload Identity provider; observed in proxy logs an occasional skip of normalization step under high load.
impact_analysis: Approximately 12% of nightly runs in analytics-prod and 9% in analytics-staging failed first-attempts over the past 7 days, leading to ~8 manual reruns. No customer-facing impact identified. Operational overhead: Pager/SRE time and runbook executions. Potential security risk if we relax role trust conditions incorrectly; must be careful to normalize tokens rather than widen trust policy.
workaround: Manual rerun of the failed CronJob pod triggers a new token request which usually succeeds. Temporary mitigation implemented: added an internal retry gate in the scheduler to do 3 fast retries with jitter before marking job run failed (deployed to staging on 2026-03-13).
proposed_next_steps: 1) Short-term: Update token-exchange proxy to enforce deterministic normalization of GCP token identity claims (prefer 'email' claim when present, fall back to fully-qualified service account email). Deploy canary to staging and monitor for 48h.
2) Medium-term: Expand unit/integration tests for proxy to cover both GKE metadata tokens and Workload Identity tokens under concurrent loads.
3) Long-term: Update AWS role trust Condition to accept both expected token formats but scoped tightly to analytics project (only if security review approves).
4) Run IAM policy simulation in AWS console for both token variants to confirm no unexpected principals are allowed.
5) Create a follow-up ticket to instrument token-exchange metrics (token_format, normalization_skips) and add alert on >1% normalization_skips per hour.
